Web productssince 2012

I'm Gorka Molero. I've been building for the web for fourteen years and worked as a senior frontend engineer and UI lead on Roadie, Pickzen and Typeshare.

AI agentssince 2023

Since 2023 most of my work has been with AI. At Roadie I built the AI infrastructure, the MCP server and much of the context layer for agents. I build interfaces people use to work with agents and systems that keep them reliable, and I make games and media with AI. Here's a selection.

components-narration--default:
"The February fog rolls thick over the Massachusetts coastline as your bus groans to a halt at the edge of a world that seems to have forgotten the twentieth century exists. The driver — a gaunt man with darting eyes — doesn't look at you when he mutters, 'End of the line.'… The letter you carry feels heavier in your coat pocket. Its message remains legible: 'Come to Innsmouth. The sea remembers what the land forgets.'"
The narrator's actual prose, verbatim from the session above — the AI writing, not a scripted line.
components-pointslist--default:
• Design a purpose-built language (StoryScript) instead of a JSON schema or an off-the-shelf engine — plain text that an LLM can write, a human can read, and the runtime executes directly with no compile step.
  • Separate authoring primitives from runtime behavior, so a scene can be edited and played from the same source of truth.
  • React for tooling, Phaser for execution — each framework does the job it is good at instead of one doing both badly.
  • Treat AI as a production pipeline, not a chat box bolted onto the game — and extract alpha with a white/black difference matte instead of background removal, so skin tones on a grey backdrop come out clean.
  • Build a real game (Shadow Over Innsmouth) to validate the system, rather than shipping an abstract engine with no proof it holds up.
  • Verify scenes in a local browser harness — movement, perspective scale, hotspot coverage, and door transitions get checked against the running game.

components-worksection--default:
openroadie

Roadie · 2026 · TypeScript, React, Vite, Tailwind, React Flow, TanStack Query, Node, Express, Postgres, Redis, Vercel AI SDK, MCP, Storybook, Vitest, Playwright, Docker

The open-source context layer that came out of Roadie. It builds a graph of an organisation from the tools it already uses, around forty of them from GitHub and Jira to PagerDuty and Slack, and serves it to AI agents over MCP. Agents can only act through deterministic actions an admin has defined, with every call scoped to the caller.

I wrote much of its foundation and designed and built its interfaces, from the data-source pipelines and the relationship maps in React Flow to agent-led onboarding. Its design system, @roadiehq/ui, which I co-led, has about sixty components in Storybook, including the AI elements for agent conversations.
